note: rc67: both cells moved by the dung reference (see note_dung_reference_2026_10_13 on each). PREVIOUS NOTE | rc60: 457.188 -> 560.754 at FY2015-16 and 213.542 -> 226.790 at FY2023-24. The step is the oil- and diesel-fired main-activity power SO2 that entered the panel from data/activity/power/power_so2_admission.csv - 103.566 and 13.248 Gg - and nothing else moved: no input changed and no other sector gained a row. The decline steepens from -53.3 to -59.6 percent, because furnace-oil generation collapsed across the panel and the admission is weighted to the early years. outputs/pakemis_air_power_admission_bridge.csv is the per-year account. ITEM 3: 560.754 -> 560.757 at FY2015-16 and 226.790 -> 226.806 at FY2023-24, national SO2 in Gg. The whole of that step is ind_ldo_boiler leaving the road-diesel sulfur proxy for its own PSI grade row (ldo_psi_grade, 0.53 percent central under a 1.8 percent ceiling): the register had justified the proxy on the grounds that no Pakistani LDO specification was held, and one is. Industrial light diesel oil is under two parts in ten thousand of national industrial SO2, so the repair is correct and is not a lever - it moves the later years more than the early ones because the proxy it replaced stepped down to 500 ppm at FY2018 while LDO's own grade did not. Nothing else moved: the brick-coal and furnace-oil centrals are unchanged and their disagreements are published unadopted in outputs/pakemis_fuel_sulfur_decision.csv. rc63: 560.757 -> 699.210 at FY2015-16 and 226.806 -> 246.002 at FY2023-24, national SO2 in Gg. The national nine-year decline steepens from 59.6 to 64.8 percent. TWO SULFUR CENTRALS MOVED, both adopted on published verdicts in outputs/pakemis_fuel_sulfur_decision.csv. Brick-kiln coal went 4.5 -> 4.643 percent, basis field_range -> measured_avg: the mean of the three as-fired Pakistani kiln-coal analyses held, replacing the geometric middle of two Punjab coalfields' RESOURCE ranges. That is +3.2 percent on brick and is not why it was adopted - the basis is. Furnace oil went 1.3229 -> 3.0 percent for the three power RFO classes, which now cite the industry row: one national fuel had carried two centrals 2.27x apart, and the held import grade split (85.3-100 percent high-sulphur) chose between them. That is +126.8 percent on power RFO and is most of this step. NEITHER STREAM'S OWN TREND CHANGED - industry falls 59.8 percent before and after, power 78.3 percent before and after. The aggregate steepened because power's share of the opening year rose from 23 to 40 percent and power declines faster than the total. A sulfur value is a flat multiplier within a stream; re-weighting streams whose paths differ is what moves an aggregate trend.
